<!-- Generated by tools/build.py from spec/rites/retro.md. Do not edit by hand. -->

Run the retrospective for: $ARGUMENTS

Agents do not learn between sessions. A retrospective whose output is a shared
understanding produces nothing, because there is no head for the understanding
to live in.

> **If the retrospective did not produce a diff, it did not happen.**

## Gather evidence

Look at what actually occurred this sprint, not at impressions:

- stories rejected at review, and why
- stories sent back from checkpoint as loops
- estimates that diverged by more than one step
- diffs rejected for touching files outside their package
- any false done that reached review

## Convert each finding into a rule change

For every recurring finding, write the **diff** to a rule file:

| Finding | Where the diff lands |
|---|---|
| Agent misread project conventions | `CLAUDE.md` |
| A role overstepped or under-delivered | that subagent's definition |
| A false done slipped through | the Definition of Done |
| Estimates keep diverging on one story shape | the estimation scale |

Delegate the writing to the `scrum-master` subagent — it owns the rule body,
the fourth artifact.

## Close the loop

End with the concrete diff, applied or ready to apply. A retro that ends in a
list of intentions has produced nothing that survives the session.

If no finding justifies a rule change, say that explicitly and say why — that
is a legitimate outcome, and it is different from having found nothing.
